share.title: Share "{{name}}"
share.description: Recipients act through this connection without seeing the stored kubeconfig. Read = browse resources, view YAML & stream logs. Write is reserved for a later revision (exec / apply).

sidebar.heading: Kubernetes clusters
sidebar.deleteDescription: The connection and every grant under it are removed from all backends. This does not touch the Kubernetes cluster itself. This cannot be undone.
sidebar.kubeconfigEmpty: No kubeconfig is stored for this connection.

dialog.description: The kubeconfig is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. Only you, the owner, can download it again — people you share the connection with never see it. Exec credential plugins are disabled server-side.
dialog.kubeconfigPlaceholderStored: •••• (stored — paste or upload a new kubeconfig to replace)
dialog.kubeconfigHelp: Paste the whole kubeconfig YAML or upload the file. Contexts are parsed to populate the selector below.
dialog.contextPlaceholder: paste a kubeconfig to detect contexts
dialog.defaultContextHelp: The context the explorer opens on. You can switch contexts inside the explorer.
dialog.backendLocalDesc: Talks to the cluster from your local machine. Required for 127.0.0.1 / LAN API servers.
dialog.backendRemoteDesc: Talks to the cluster from the team backend. Use for prod / staging behind VPN.
dialog.backendNote: The connection is saved to BOTH backends — the kubeconfig gets encrypted with each BE's own key. Pick which one this connection defaults to.
dialog.skipTlsHelp: Accept any API-server certificate. Insecure — dev / self-signed only.
dialog.allowedNamespacesHelp: Comma-separated. When set, the explorer only lists resources in these namespaces. Leave blank for all.
dialog.allowExecPluginsHelp: For kubeconfigs that authenticate via an exec plugin (AWS EKS / GKE).
dialog.execPluginsWarning: Runs the kubeconfig's auth plugin (e.g. <0>aws</0> / <1>gcloud</1>) on this machine. Only enable for clusters you trust; the plugin binary must be installed locally. Ignored on the hosted PatchMan backend.
dialog.prometheusServiceHelp: Optional. Pin the in-cluster Prometheus as "namespace/service:port" to serve historical pod metrics via the API-server proxy. Leave blank to auto-discover.
dialog.readSecretHostsHelp: The service map reads the Secrets a workload references (e.g. DATABASE_URL) and keeps only the host:port. Values never leave PatchMan's backend. Needs 'get secrets' permission.

podMetrics.needServer: Pod metrics need metrics-server installed in this cluster.
podMetrics.noMetricsYet: No metrics for this pod yet.
podMetrics.liveNote: Live — sampled every few seconds since you opened this. metrics-server keeps no history; longer-range graphs would need a metrics backend (e.g. Prometheus).
podMetrics.histEmpty: No historical data for this pod in the selected range.
podMetrics.histWarn: Historical metrics unavailable: {{error}}. Showing live samples instead.

apply.title: Apply changes <mono>· {{target}}</mono>
apply.description: Server-Side Apply (field manager <mono>patchman</mono>). Review the dry-run diff before committing.
apply.conflictsHint: These fields are owned by another manager. Use Force apply to overwrite them.
apply.noFieldChanges: No field-level changes from the live object.
apply.forceApplyDescription: Force apply overwrites fields currently owned by other field managers. Their conflicting values will be replaced by this manifest. This can clobber changes made by controllers or other users.

overview.selectClusterContext: Select a cluster and context to see the overview.
overview.metricsUnavailable: Metrics unavailable — install metrics-server for CPU/memory

explorer.noClusters: No clusters yet. Add one from the Kubernetes sidebar tab.
explorer.nsDisabledOverview: Namespace doesn't apply to the cluster Overview
explorer.nsDisabledClusterScoped: This resource is cluster-scoped — namespaces don't apply
explorer.localShellTitle: Opens a terminal on your machine with this cluster's kubeconfig
explorer.localShellTitleDesktopOnly: Opens a terminal on your machine with this cluster's kubeconfig (desktop only)
explorer.forwardsTitle: Active port-forwards running on your machine
explorer.forwardsTitleDesktopOnly: Port-forward runs on your machine (desktop only)
explorer.noActiveForwards: No active forwards. Start one from a Pod or Service.
explorer.selectClusterExplore: Select a cluster to explore resources.
explorer.showingFirst: Showing first {{shown}} of {{total}} — use the filter above to narrow.
explorer.metricsNeedServer: Pod metrics need metrics-server installed in the cluster

actions.reasonPortForwardDesktop: Port-forward runs on your machine (desktop only)
actions.deleteDescription: Permanently delete {{kind}} {{target}}. This cannot be undone.
actions.restartDescription: Trigger a rolling restart of {{kind}} {{name}}? Pods are recreated with zero downtime per the rollout strategy.
actions.cordonDescription: Mark {{name}} unschedulable. Running pods stay; no new pods are scheduled.
actions.drainDescription: Cordon {{name}} and evict its pods (DaemonSet + mirror pods are skipped). Workloads reschedule elsewhere.
actions.triggerDescription: Create a Job now from {{name}}'s template.

scale.title: Scale {{kind}}
scale.toZeroHint: Scaling to 0 stops all pods — you'll be asked to confirm.
scale.toZeroDescription: Scaling {{name}} to 0 stops all of its pods.

portForward.title: Port forward
portForward.subtitle: {{kind}} · {{target}}
portForward.localPortHint: Blank picks a free port on 127.0.0.1.
portForward.errLocalPort: Local port must be a positive number.

logs.previousTip: Logs of the previous (terminated) container instance — useful after a crash or restart.
logs.tailTip: Lines to load — applies on Enter or after a pause
